gaps.sentence: Is there a reason ___ you're behaving so strangely?
gaps.explanation: 'A reason why ...' asks about the cause; the other relative words cannot express reason.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge, ___ cost two billion euros, opened last month.
gaps.hint: thing + extra information after a comma
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces non-defining clauses about things; 'that' is forbidden there.

gaps.sentence: My colleague Anna, ___ joined us in May, has already been promoted.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to Anna; non-defining clauses never use 'that'.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The scientist ___ research we cited has won the Nobel Prize.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession: the scientist whose research…

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ I'm calling is to confirm your appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' introduces the explanation or cause; the other options do not express reason.
